results.title: 2026 commercial real estate outlook | Deloitte Insights
results.content: Despite inbound capital dipping in recent quarters, the United States remains the top source of outbound global investment capital, with activity in the first quarter of 2025 returning numbers slightly ahead of the five-year average.[10](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html#endnote-10)This trend could strengthen in 2025 and 2026, as US asset managers have ample dry powder[11](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html#endnote-11)—property sales are up year over year, and a new executive order could allow individual retirement accounts to invest in private markets, potentially unlocking US$12 trillion in capital.[12](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html#endnote-12)Globally, 75% of European and Asia-Pacific respondents expect to increase real estate investment in the next 18 months, especially in India (86%), Canada (80%), and France (78%). Global fundraising through early 2025 is also on track to surpass totals in the previous two years.[13](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html#endnote-13)Notably, private credit strategies have drawn significant fundraising interest, accounting for a third of new capital raised.[14](https://www.deloitte.com/us/en/insights/industry/financial-services/commercial-real-estate-outlook.html#endnote-14)With relatively high interest rates and debt set to mature in the next few years, investors and asset managers may look to capitalize on emerging opportunities in the real estate debt markets.
